## What we know

- **Name:** 石道 (圆明园西南-清漪园北-青龙桥) (S241, S240, S02, S05, S03, S22 · confidence A)
- **In English:** Paved road from the 圆明园 west past 清漪园's north wall to 青龙桥 and 静明园 (S241, S240, S02, S05, S03, S22)
- **What it was:** a road outside the garden walls (S241, S240, S02, S05, S03, S22 · confidence A)
- **In 1860:** in use; in 1860 'blocked up at intervals with sand and stone barriers' (S241 p.332) (S241, S240, S02, S05, S03, S22)
- **Width drawn:** 8 m (S241, S240, S02, S05, S03, S22)
- **Where:** C: today's 颐和园路 west part (osm ways of 颐和园路 at 40.0005-40.0042) from the 西苑 bend to 青龙桥 (S241, S240, S02, S05, S03, S22 · confidence C)
- **Note:** Swinhoe pp.332-333: paved road from the park's left wall 'passes close under the wall of ... the Wan-show-yuen', through 青龙桥, round 静明园. Wolseley pp.284-285: stone archway, shops both sides for half a mile, 'The paved road ends at the gates of the Golden Palace'. [j85:28a-28b] 石道迤邐至青龍橋即逹清漪園之輦道也; [j86:9a] 東宫門外石路二南達香山寺. Also: Tour du monde 1864 sketch read, fit rms 427 m (schematic) (the road from the gate court west to the 'Village' by 万寿山), 971 m from the point used. (S241, S240, S02, S05, S03, S22)
